Rashi on Bava Metzia 30b:11:1.hebrew: זה בית חייהם - ללמוד להם אומנות להתפרנס בו. חוקות ותורות כתיבי ברישיה דקרא:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 30b:11:1.english: That [is] their livelihood - To teach them a trade with which to sustain themselves. Statutes and laws are [already] written at the beginning of the verse.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 30b:14:1.english: Should they adjudicate arbitrary decisions - [This is asked] in astonishment.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 30b:14:2.hebrew: דמגיזתא - גוזאי הדנין ביסורים ובחזקה, וחבירו בבבא קמא (דף קיד.) דדייני בגזתיא:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 30b:14:2.english: Of arbitrary decisions [demagizeta] - Coercive judges who judge with torments and with force; and its counterpart [is] in Bava Kamma (114a): "who judge with coercion [begaztaya]."

Rashi on Bava Metzia 30b:15:1.english: Which is lost property - In the Gemara, it explains [this].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 30b:15:2.hebrew: איזו זו אבידה - ואינו חייב להחזיר, שמדעת הניחוה שם:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 30b:15:2.english: Which is this lost property - And he is not obligated to return [it], for they left it there intentionally.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 30b:15:3.english: Running among the vineyards - For it gets injured.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 30b:16:1.hebrew: לא יאמר לו תן לי סלע - שבטלתי ממלאכתי, שיאמר לו: אם עשית מלאכתך, היית מרבה טורח; עכשיו לפי מה שטרחת, טול:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 30b:16:1.english: He shall not say to him: Give me a sela - [claiming,] "because I was idle from my work," for [the owner] will say to him: "If you had done your work, you would have exerted much effort; now, according to what you have exerted, take [your wage]."

Rashi on Bava Metzia 30b:16:2.english: As a laborer - [This] is explained in the Gemara.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 30b:16:3.hebrew: אם יש שם בית דין - אם נוח לו לטרוח יותר כדי להרבות שכר, ואינו חפץ ליבטל ממלאכתו, מה יעשה? אם יש שם שלשה בני אדם, יתנה בפניהם ויאמר: ראו שאני משתכר כך וכך, ואי איפשי ליבטל ליטול שכר מועט. אני אשיב, אם תאמרו שאטול שכר משלם:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 30b:16:3.english: If there is a court there - If he prefers to exert himself more in order to increase [his] wage, and he does not wish to be idle from his work, what should he do? If there are three people there, he should stipulate before them and say: "See that I earn such-and-such, and I do not wish to be idle [from my work] to take a small wage. I will return [the lost item], if you say that I shall take full wages."

Rashi on Bava Metzia 30b:17:1.english: Principle - A general [case of a] lost item that is proven to be there without the owner's knowledge.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 30b:18:1.hebrew: ולעולם - בתמיה, וכי אף אם ימצאנה שם לעולם, נאמר מדעת היא? וכי דרך שלא להכניס:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 30b:18:1.english: And forever - [This is asked] in astonishment: even if one finds it there forever, shall we say it is [there] intentionally? Is it customary not to bring [an animal] inside?

Rashi on Bava Metzia 30b:19:1.english: In the early morning - Before dawn.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 30b:19:2.english: Darkness - That it grew dark [in the] evening.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 30b:1:1.english: There shall be no needy among you - Do not bring yourself to poverty.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 30b:3:1.hebrew: הכישה - זה שאינו לפי כבודו, אם הכישה הכאה אחת להשיבה, נתחייב בה לאהדורה, הואיל והתחיל:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 30b:3:1.english: He struck it - This [person], for whom [returning it] is not in accordance with his dignity: if he struck it one blow to return it, he has become obligated in it to return it, since he began.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 30b:3:2.english: Kala [a clod of dirt] - Mote [a clod of earth] in Old French.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 30b:4:1.english: It is his manner to return [it] in the field - For there are not so many onlookers there and he is not embarrassed.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 30b:4:2.hebrew: ואין דרכו בעיר - שהוא בוש משכיניו, והוא מצא בשדה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 30b:4:2.english: And it is not his manner [to return it] in the city - For he is ashamed before his neighbors, and he found [it] in the field.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 30b:4:3.english: What is [the law] - That he should be obligated to return it.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 30b:4:4.english: He is not obligated - to begin returning it in the field.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 30b:4:5.hebrew: וכיון דאיחייב - שהזיזה ממקומה, חייב אף בעיר:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 30b:4:5.english: And once he is obligated - [In that] he moved it from its place [in the field], he is obligated even in the city.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 30b:5:1.hebrew: פורק וטוען - פורק משא מן החמור וטוען עליו, דכתיב: "עזוב תעזוב", "הקם תקים":
Rashi on Bava Metzia 30b:5:1.english: Unloads and loads - [He] unloads a burden from the donkey and loads [it] upon it, as it is written: "You shall surely help unload [it]" [Exodus 23:5], [and] "You shall surely help lift [it] up" [Deuteronomy 22:4].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 30b:6:1.english: A bundle of wood - A load of wood.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 30b:6:2.english: And was resting - [He was] standing to rest.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 30b:6:3.english: Lift [it] for me - Load [it upon] me.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 30b:7:1.english: He again acquired them - That man went back and took possession of them from ownerless [property].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 30b:8:1.hebrew: הפקר לעניים הוי הפקר - אע"ג שלא הפקירו אלא לעניים, הוי הפקר למפטר מן המעשר:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 30b:8:1.english: [Property declared] ownerless for the poor is ownerless - Even though he declared it ownerless only for the poor, it is [considered] ownerless so as to be exempt from tithes.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 30b:14:1.hebrew: לא חרבה כו' - ואם תאמר דביומא (דף ט:) אמר מפני שנאת חנם, וי"ל דהא והא גרמא:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 30b:14:1.english: "[Jerusalem] was not destroyed," etc. - And if you will say that in Yoma (9b) it says [that it was destroyed] because of baseless hatred, one can answer that both this and that caused [it].

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 30b:15:1.english: Which is lost property - [This means] that one understands that the owners do not know that it is there.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 30b:2:1.hebrew: אלא לזקן ואינו לפי כבודו - וא"ת: תיפוק ליה מ"ולאחותו", דכבוד הבריות דוחה מילת בנו ושחיטת פסחו? וי"ל: כבוד הבריות דמת מצוה חמיר טפי, שמוטל בבזיון, פן יסריח או יאכלוהו כלבים. אע"ג דבפ' מי שמתו (ברכות דף כ. ושם ד"ה שב) מוכח דאי הוה כלאים שב ואל תעשה היה נדחה מפני כבוד הבריות, היינו משום דערום הוי גנות ובזיון גדול, כדאמר (יבמות דף סג:): "אין לך משוקץ יותר מאותו שהוא מהלך ערום". ומהכא לא ידעי' דדחי אלא ממונא, אבל איסורא כמו פסח ומילה וגם כרת — לא: [וע' תוס' שבועות ל: ד"ה אבל]:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 30b:2:1.english: "Rather, [it is needed] for an elderly person and it is not in keeping with his dignity" - And if you ask: let it be derived from "and for his sister" [Numbers 6:7, from which we learn] that human dignity overrides the circumcision of one's son and the slaughtering of one's Paschal offering? One can answer: the human dignity of a met mitzvah [an unattended corpse] is more severe, for it lies in disgrace, lest it decompose or dogs eat it. Even though in the chapter Mi Shemeito (Berakhot 20a, and there, s.v. shev) it is proven that if [removing] kilayim were [a matter of] "sit and do nothing" [i.e., passive], it would be overridden by human dignity, that is because being naked is a great shame and disgrace, as it says (Yevamot 63b): "You have nothing more loathsome than one who walks naked." Whereas from here [the case of a lost item] we only know that [human dignity] overrides monetary matters, but [that it overrides] a prohibition such as the Paschal offering and circumcision, which also [carry the penalty of] karet — we do not [derive from here]. [And see Tosafot on Shevuot 30b, s.v. aval]:

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 30b:6:1.hebrew: אפקרה - שלא יכשלו בני אדם בלא תגזול. וא"ת: הא אמר בפ' אין בין המודר (נדרים דף מה.) "אין הפקר אלא בפני שלשה"? וי"ל דהכא נמי הוו שלשה. אי נמי, דאורייתא בלא שלשה נמי הוי הפקר; והא דאמר שלהי פ"ק דשבת (דף יח: ושם ד"ה דמפקרא): "גיגית, נר וקדירה אפקורי מפקר להו", אע"ג דליכא שלשה — התם אנן סהדי דמפקר להו בלבו, שלא יעשה איסור שביתת כלים:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 30b:6:1.english: He declared it ownerless - So that people would not stumble into [violating] "You shall not steal." And if you ask: Behold, [the Gemara] says in the chapter [entitled] Ein Bein HaMudar (Nedarim 45a): "A declaration of ownerlessness [is valid] only in the presence of three [people]"? One can say that here too there were three [people]. Alternatively, by Torah law, even without three [people] it is [valid] ownerless property; and [as for] that which [the Gemara] says at the end of the first chapter of Shabbat (18b, and there s.v. de'mafkera): "[Regarding] a vat, a lamp, and a pot, he certainly declares them ownerless," even though there are not three [people] — there, we are witnesses that he declares them ownerless in his heart, so that he will not commit the prohibition of the resting of utensils [on Shabbat].
